One day, He Jin went into the wild to pick Qianghuang flowers. The sound of a wooden arrow cutting through the air rushed toward her face. She dropped to the ground immediately, escaping the fatal blow. 
A man ran over from not far away, dressed like a hunter. He Jin pulled the wooden arrow out of the sand and handed it to him. 
Startled by He Jin's gaze, the hunter mumbled: "I thought there were wolves around, so I shot the arrow." 

"Then, do I look like a wolf?" 
"Such a fine lady, how could you be a wolf?" 
"Thank you. Next time, see carefully before you shoot." 
"I know! I was muddled. Wolves always come in packs, how could there be just one…" 

Before he finished speaking, the hunter suddenly shuddered. He drew his bow with trembling hands and turned around, only to see a man not far away staring firmly at him, walking slowly closer. 
So the other wolf had arrived late! 
The hunter barely had time to glance back and say a hasty farewell to He Jin before fleeing in panic. 

The wind picked up again. Feeling the threat behind him had disappeared, the hunter looked back. 
The two figures gradually blurred and faded in the wind and sand, shrinking into a distant dot, never to be found again.

Zhang Wanshi was granted the title of Grand Artisan at the age of nineteen—an age when diligent disciples in the sect were just barely qualified to enter the inner circle.
At that time, Zhang Wanshi was at the peak of his brilliance, claiming to master all mechanisms and believing he could be a teacher to countless future disciples without borrowing the names of past sages. He insisted on using his own name as his title, drawing much criticism.
Later, when Crow was granted his name, Zhang Wanshi was already waiting outside the hall.
"It just occurred to me—now that you've received your name, our master ought to give you a gift. But since our master is rarely home, I’ll stand in for him. Here, newly forged." A sharp sword, sheathed in an antique scabbard. "The Sword of Triumph."

Zhang Wanshi knew his junior brother would surely return victorious.
And Crow understood that his senior brother never imposed his own ambitions on others.
